review.summary: The GltB Ntn-amidotransferase center hydrolyzes glutamine for the coupled reaction.
review.reason: Retain the inherited glutaminase proposal as a direct subreaction supported by the target type-2 amidotransferase domain and the experimentally characterized homolog active center. GO:0004359 describes glutamine hydrolysis to glutamate/ammonium; channeling the ammonia to the adjacent synthase site does not negate that chemistry. This is not an assertion of unregulated free-ammonia release or of the distinct periplasmic glutaminase/asparaginase whose expression is affected by gltB mutation.

supported_by.supporting_text: Channeling of the ammonia intermediate is brought about by an internal tunnel of 31 A length, which runs from the site of L-glutamine hydrolysis to the site of L-glutamate synthesis.

retired_proposals.reason: Retire this inherited reviewer-authored standalone glutaminase proposal. Glutamine hydrolysis is retained as the coupled large-chain mechanism within NADPH-dependent GOGAT, with contributes_to_molecular_function GO:0004355 used consistently across all four large chains. No machine-sourced claim is removed and no equivalent proposals are added merely for coverage.
